Independent check: Benzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen, so concentrated NaOH causes the Cannizzaro reaction, forming sodium benzoate and benzyl alcohol.
solution:
Benzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen, so it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction in concentrated NaOH:
$$2\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}+\text{NaOH}\rightarrow\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COONa}+\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$
The products are sodium benzoate and benzyl alcohol.
